checkpoints.prompt: After an operations administrator signs in to AWS, only a specific S3 operation returns AccessDenied. Select one item to check first.

choices.text: Check the calling principal, operation, target resource, and the policies that apply to them.
choices.explanation: An operation denial after successful authentication calls for isolating authorization.

choices.text: Change the password repeatedly.
choices.explanation: This does not investigate the cause of the denial after successful authentication.

checkpoints.prompt: An operations engineer grants a batch running on AWS permission to write to S3 only during the three hours it is running. Select one way of granting permissions that meets this requirement.

checkpoints.prompt: An operations engineer is investigating why an AWS API call from an application using an IAM role was denied. The policy attached to the role allows the call. Choose two other things to check.

choices.text: Check whether an explicit deny applies to the request.

choices.text: Check the ultimately permitted operation, including resource-based policies, applicable conditions, and permissions boundaries.
choices.explanation: The controls are evaluated together.

choices.text: Ignore Deny because Allow is present.
choices.explanation: An explicit deny cannot be ignored.

blocks.label: Overview
blocks.text: Separate who performs the operation, what is permitted, and who can assume the role when evaluating IAM.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Distinguish authentication, authorization, IAM roles, and least privilege when evaluating a configuration.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Separate authentication from authorization to isolate the cause of a denial.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Identify the principal and the role-assumption conditions.

blocks.label: Learning objectives
blocks.text: Determine effective permissions by combining Allow, explicit Deny, and conditions.

blocks.label: Learning objective
blocks.text: Narrow operations, targets, and time periods to the minimum necessary.

blocks.label: Authentication and authorization answer different questions.
blocks.text: Authentication verifies who the principal sending a request is. Passwords and multi-factor authentication strengthen verification of the principal.

blocks.label: Authentication and authorization answer different questions.
blocks.text: Authorization determines whether a verified principal can perform a specific action on a resource. If an S3 operation returns AccessDenied after a successful sign-in, check the authorization principal, action, resource, and policies.

steps.label: Authentication and authorization answer different questions.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: The user's sign-in succeeded, but GetObject for a specific bucket was denied.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Separate successful authentication from denied authorization.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Identify the requested action and target resource.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Evaluate the applicable Allow, Deny, and condition.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can investigate the rejection layer without hiding the authorization issue through password changes or public settings.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: Passing multi-factor authentication lets you operate every bucket.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: Strengthening authentication does not automatically add permissions to authorization policies.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: Authentication is who you are; authorization is what you can do.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: With AccessDenied, proceed to evaluate the request and policies.

blocks.label: Principal and role assumption conditions
blocks.text: A principal is an entity that requests AWS operations. This includes people, applications running on EC2, and AWS services.

blocks.label: Principal and role assumption conditions
blocks.text: IAM roles have trust policies and permissions policies. A trust policy defines who can assume the role, while a permissions policy defines the operations allowed after assumption. STS issues temporary credentials.

blocks.label: Scenario
blocks.text: Allow the batch to write to S3 for only 3 hours.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Identify the principal that runs the batch.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Use a trust policy so that only that principal can assume the role.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Use a permissions policy to allow only the required bucket, prefix, and action.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can separate the principal from its permissions without distributing long-term access keys.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: If you put a principal in a role's trust policy, that principal can perform all AWS operations.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: A trust policy defines the conditions for assuming a role, while operations after assumption are controlled separately by permission policies.

blocks.label: Takeaway
blocks.text: A principal is not limited to a person; it also includes a running application.

blocks.label: Takeaway
blocks.text: Check the trust policy and permissions policy separately.

blocks.label: Review explicit Deny, not just Allow
blocks.text: IAM effective permissions are evaluated by combining the requested principal, action, resource, and condition with the multiple policies that apply. Having one Allow does not necessarily establish permission.

blocks.label: Review explicit Deny, not just Allow
blocks.text: An explicit Deny that applies to the request takes precedence over Allow. Check the scope of applicable policies, including resource policies, identity policies, permissions boundaries, and Organizations controls.

steps.label: Review explicit Deny, not just Allow

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: There is an Allow for S3:GetObject, but the request received AccessDenied for the same target.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: Fix the actual principal, action, and resource.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Look for the applicable Deny and condition.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Evaluate the necessary Allow permissions and the permissions boundary together.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: You can identify the responsibility for the denial without bypassing it by allowing every operation.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: If you find an Allow, you can ignore Deny.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: An applicable explicit Deny takes precedence over Allow.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: Do not determine effective permissions from Allow alone.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: Specify the resources and conditions to which Deny applies.

blocks.label: Least privilege and short-lived credentials
blocks.text: Least privilege is the principle of allowing a principal to perform only the actions required for its work on the resources it needs, under the necessary conditions and for the necessary duration.

blocks.label: Least privilege and short-lived credentials
blocks.text: Issue credentials for the execution role temporarily, and do not place long-term access keys in source code or shared configurations. Review actual usage to reduce or update permissions.

blocks.label: Situation
blocks.text: An image-conversion Lambda reads images under a specific prefix and writes the artifacts.

blocks.label: Step 1
blocks.text: List the required GetObject and PutObject operations.

blocks.label: Step 2
blocks.text: Limit the target bucket and prefix.

blocks.label: Step 3
blocks.text: Associate the execution role with Lambda, and do not store long-term keys.

blocks.label: Conclusion
blocks.text: This limits the impact of a leak and excessive permissions.

blocks.label: This is incorrect
blocks.text: When it does not work, grant administrator permissions for all AWS services.

blocks.label: Correction
blocks.text: Identify the requests and denials, and add only the necessary action, resource, and condition.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: Limit the operations, resources, conditions, and duration.

blocks.label: Key takeaway
blocks.text: Do not share human keys with applications.
